[00:00] Maia Chen: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the Springboard all-hands. We're at about 58 minutes, we've got a packed agenda, I'll try to keep it tight. Quick logistics: recording is on, questions at the end in Q&A.
[00:28] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[00:35] Maia Chen: First up, the high level - why this quarter feels different. We have product-market moments across Dedicated and Private where teams are actually requesting predictable latency and hard SLAs not just throughput. that shift matters for our go-to-market.
[01:05] Jonah Park: I'll show the product priorities in a sec but to summarize: shipped features and the Optimize toolkit are the centerpieces. Optimize is our lever for customers who need cost/perf tuning without switching models.
[01:36] Ravi Singh: Quick tech note — infra is stable, p99 latency across hosted is down ~12% MoM; p95 is down too, and we saw unit cost improvements after kernel improvements. small caveat, some traffic patterns spiked on Tuesday which stressed the autoscaler, we'll talk about the mitigation.
[02:10] Elena Cruz: The autoscaler incident — we have a postmortem in the ops channel. TL;DR: batching threshold math + a bad default for warmup caused a transient backlog. We're changing the defaults and adding a canary for burst scaling.
[02:47] Maia Chen: Hiring update — we're approving 18 roles for Q2, prioritized SRE and SEs for dedicated customers. Heads of hiring, please sync with People.
[03:10] Speaker 2: applause
[03:20] Samira Patel: Sales & growth quick note: pipeline for Dedicated increased 30% this month, largely mid-market companies and a handful of enterprises starting security conversations. We closed two pilot deals last week.
[03:45] Maia Chen: Great. On the product roadmap — Jonah?
[03:52] Jonah Park: Thanks, Maia. Slide one — roadmap themes: predictability, enterprise controls, and cost optimization. Predictability maps to Dedicated and Private improvements: better autoscaling policies, predictable slot-based capacity, and region affinity.
[04:20] Jonah Park: For enterprise controls — we're shipping RBAC improvements, audit log retention options, fine-grained model pinning and a simpler KMS integration path. We heard loud feedback on KMS and HSM options so we're prioritizing that for Private.
[04:56] Speaker 3: hm, KMS spelling sounded like 'K-M-S' in notes
[05:02] Jonah Park: Sorry, yes KMS and HSM support — apologies the transcript might say other names. We expect a beta for Private KMS in Q3.
[05:20] Jonah Park: Optimize — this is the set of UI + runner recommendations we believe will save customers 15-30% on tokens with little quality loss: better quantization suggestions and automatic prefix caching.
[05:44] Ravi Singh: On the runtime side, Optimize will glue into our KV cache and smarter batching; note that some older models behave differently with quantized kernels and we'll surface per-model guidance.
[06:10] Maia Chen: Questions about quality regressions?
[06:14] Elena Cruz: We're coupling the rollout with evals — each optimization has a guardrail test against critical prompt sets. If quality regressed we have automatic rollback. The eval infra is being expanded to hold more customer prompts in an encrypted store.
[06:42] Speaker 4: (crosstalk) what about model fallbacks?
[06:48] Ravi Singh: We do automated fallback to a compatible variant when quantization causes issues, and we ship canary routes to route small percentage of traffic through new kernels.
[07:10] Maia Chen: Next, metrics snapshot — finance slide. Samira?
[07:18] Samira Patel: Quick numbers, top-level: ARR growth is accelerating, net retention ticked up slightly. Hosted usage revenue grew 24% QoQ; Dedicated contract TCV is increasing but with longer sales cycles. Cost is still the main focus — we improved GPU utilization across fleets by a few points.
[07:49] Maia Chen: Reminder — this doesn't mean cut corners on reliability. The improvements are in orchestration and packing, not in disabling safety checks.
[08:05] Jonah Park: Roadmap timeline: May — rollout of RBAC & audit logs; June — first Dedicated performance ramps & SLA definition; July — Optimize public beta. The team should expect more detailed PRDs in the product channel next week.
[08:34] Speaker 5: question: SLA and legal?
[08:38] Maia Chen: Good point — legal is working with Sales on SLA templates. We'll standardize SLA tiers; baseline SLA will be for Dedicated, hosted will have differentiated tiers.
[08:58] Ravi Singh: From a reliability standpoint, our goal is 99.9% regionally for Dedicated; hosted higher-level SLOs will be balanced with cost. We'll publish the SLOs and burn-rate alerts so customers can see expected behaviors.
[09:20] Elena Cruz: Also implementing better tracing so root cause times are reduced, that reduces MTTR and supports SLA claims.
[09:36] Maia Chen: Now on compliance — Leah from Security will update us.
[09:41] Speaker 6 (Leah): Quick SOC 2 update: we've completed most control mapping, external audit scheduled for August. We need two outstanding items: role separation for a legacy billing app and stronger key rotation policies in some regions. Sales — you'll get a SOC 2 readiness doc in 48 hours.
[10:08] Samira Patel: Sales note: for large deals, customers are asking about data residency and logs retention — the Private offering is resonating. Leah, we might need a standard data residency one-pager.
[10:20] Leah: Yep, I'll coordinate with Product.
[10:25] Maia Chen: Quick highlight — customer story: RetailCo pilot reduced inference spend 22% and improved p99 latency, their engineering team specifically called out our caching.
[10:45] Speaker 7: applause

[11:12] Ravi Singh: Note — those microbenchmarks are not perfect proxies for real traffic, but they'll help customers and SEs reproduce latency regressions.

[11:45] Speaker 8: (muted) congrats
